rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Bryophytes are the simplest land plants: non-vascular, with the gametophyte as the dominant generation. They include mosses, liverworts, and hornworts. Marchantia (liverwort) and Funaria (moss) are the model organisms studied in NEB. Reproduction requires water for fertilisation; asexual reproduction occurs via gemmae and fragmentation.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Life cycle: Spore (n) → Gametophyte (n, dominant) → Gametes → Zygote (2n) → Sporophyte (2n, dependent) → Spores (n)
Gemmae: asexual, multicellular, in gemma cups
Fertilisation: Sperm (flagellated) + Egg (in archegonium) → Zygote

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Bryophytes lack TRUE roots, stems, and leaves; they have rhizoids, cauloids, and phylloids instead.  ·  The gametophyte is the DOMINANT generation in bryophytes (unlike seed plants where the sporophyte dominates).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects a labelled diagram of the Marchantia thallus (upper/lower epidermis, air chambers, rhizoids, gemma cups, antheridia, archegonia).  ·  The "amphibians of the plant kingdom" analogy is a favourite exam phrase: bryophytes live on land but need water to reproduce.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Marchantia polymorpha — liverwort, thalloid, gemma cups for asexual reproduction.  ·  Funaria hygrometrica — moss, cauloid, capsule opens with elaters in dry weather.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The sporophyte is dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition (it does not photosynthesise independently in most mosses).  ·  Fertilisation in bryophytes requires WATER for sperm to swim to the egg; this limits bryophytes to moist habitats.

rows.text: Bryophyte = no VASCULAR tissue = "Bry" (as in "no BR" in bryophyte).  ·  Gametophyte DOMINANT in bryophytes; Sporophyte DOMINANT in seed plants.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Bryophytes: non-vascular (no xylem/phloem), rhizoids instead of roots.  ·  Gametophyte (n) is the dominant, visible generation.  ·  Sporophyte (2n) is dependent on the gametophyte for nutrition.  ·  Three groups: mosses (Bryophyta), liverworts (Marchantiophyta), hornworts (Anthocerotophyta).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bryophytes were the first plants to colonise land (Devonian period, ~400 million years ago).  ·  Marchantia polymorpha is the most commonly studied liverwort in school laboratories.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Bryophytes: non-vascular land plants (no true xylem or phloem); include mosses, liverworts, and hornworts.  ·  Life cycle: alternation of generations with the gametophyte (n) as the dominant, visible generation; the sporophyte (2n) is dependent on the gametophyte.  ·  Mosses (Bryophyta): e.g., Polytrichum, Funaria; stem-like (cauloid), leaf-like (phylloid) structures; no true roots (rhizoids instead).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Alternation of generations  ·  Ecological importance  ·  Bio-indicator role

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Reproduction requires water (flagellated sperm); gemmae for asexual reproduction.  ·  Ecological role: pioneers, soil formation, moisture, air pollution indicators.  ·  Gemmae are asexual propagules in gemma cups; they are NOT spores.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Liverworts are NOT mosses: liverworts are thalloid (Marchantia) or leafy; mosses are cauloid (stem + leaf).  ·  Differentiate bryophytes from pteridophytes: bryophytes lack vascular tissue; pteridophytes have true xylem and phloem.  ·  Gemmae ≠ spores: gemmae are asexual, multicellular, in gemma cups; spores are produced meiotically in the sporangium.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise the Marchantia thallus structure (all labelled parts).  ·  Learn the bryophyte life cycle (alternation of generations).  ·  Differentiate gametophyte vs sporophyte in bryophytes.

rows.text: List ecological and economic importance of bryophytes.  ·  Know why bryophytes are called "amphibians of the plant kingdom".  ·  Bryophytes are the first group of plants to colonise terrestrial habitats.
